headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Your Home Has Low Water Pressure
articleBody:
When your water pressure drops to a trickle, it’s easy to get frustrated and maybe even try to tackle the problem yourself. While some minor issues can be DIY fixes, there are a few common mistakes people make that can actually make things worse or miss the real problem entirely. We've seen it all in our 25+ years serving Goodyear and the West Valley.

One big mistake is just ignoring the problem, hoping it will go away. Low water pressure can indicate serious underlying issues like pipe corrosion, hidden leaks, or a failing pressure regulator, which won't fix themselves and can lead to more significant damage over time. Another common misstep is replacing fixtures without investigating the cause. If the problem isn't the showerhead or faucet, you'll just have new fixtures with the same old low pressure, and you've wasted money. Don't forget to check your main shut-off valve! Many homeowners overlook this simple step, and a partially closed valve can significantly reduce pressure throughout the house.

Trying to adjust your pressure regulator without understanding how it works is another mistake. You could end up with even less pressure or, worse, damage the regulator itself, creating a different problem. Also, only attempting quick fixes like cleaning aerators and then giving up. While those are good first steps, if they don't work, it's time to call in the pros. Alpha-Plumbing Services has the experience to correctly diagnose and fix low water pressure issues, ensuring your plumbing system is healthy and efficient. We can handle everything from simple repairs to full water re-pipes if needed.
